messages:
maya: Quick sync — product asked for a clear launch gate for new model onboarding that includes a pricing sidecar and a compat shim plan. need a proposal by EOD tomorrow.

sam_k: +1. can we scope the gates? i'm thinking perf, cost delta, and semantic parity for embeddings.

diego: For perf: P50/P95 token latency targets per model family + memory/kv cache footprint. suggest P95 < 220ms on our standard 8k seq bench.

anjali: For cost sidecar: we need an estimator that reports per-request marginal cost delta vs baseline model. must surface batchability and quantization impacts.

maya: Agree. also want a customer-tier gating column (self-serve vs enterprise). enterprise can opt into pinning windows/longer grace periods.

sam_k: Draft launch gates from my side:
- bench: 95th latency threshold met on 3/3 runs
- quality: eval pass rate >= 95% on curated prompt set (or delta < 1.5% vs baseline)
- cost: marginal token cost <= +25% vs baseline; with a recommended sidecar that offers cheaper quantized variant when available
- regression: no production drift on fallback tests

maya: That feels reasonable. add a runtime-canary plan: 1% traffic for 24h, 5% for 48h, then 25% for 72h with automated rollback triggers.

diego: Rollback triggers: P95 latency increase > 30% OR error rate > 0.5% OR quality regressions on monitoring prompt set > 2% absolute.

anjali: About compat shim: onboarding must include an embedding-mapping doc when vector schema changes. example: rename dimension ordering or normalization. implement a lightweight adapter in the catalog that rewrites requests for legacy customers.

maya: + add a 'pin escape hatch' for customers pinned to older model: allow temporary dual-serve routing for 30 days while we run customer-specific fine-tune/adapter tests. ops should be able to request extension with justification.

product-ops: ops note: dual-serve lanes need a capacity budget. recommend labeling pins as 'soft' vs 'hard' so autoscaler treats soft pins as reclaimable after X days.

catalog-bot: reminder: please attach benchmarking artifacts: raw logs, 3 run summary, and canary config as JSON. failing to include these will block onboarding ticket to review.

sam_k: here's a quick canary config snippet to include in the ticket:```json
{
  "canary_steps": [{"pct":1,"duration":"24h"},{"pct":5,"duration":"48h"},{"pct":25,"duration":"72h"}],
  "rollback_conditions": {"p95_latency_pct_increase":30, "error_rate_pct":0.5, "quality_drop_abs":2}
}
```

maya: Nice. next: pricing sidecar implementation sketch — it should run offline on sampled traces and publish expected cost uplift per call, and also surface a "suggested variant" (e.g., quantized or shorter context) when uplift > 20%.

diego: Tech caveat: some models can't be quantized without quality loss. add a model-tag: "quant-tolerant" boolean and a fallback recommendation list.

anjali: For acceptance checklist in ticket: 
- bench artifacts attached
- cost sidecar report attached
- compat shim doc if schema changes
- pin & gracepath plan declared
- canary JSON included
- SLA gating for enterprise customers defined

maya: Cool — i'll write this up as an onboarding template and iterate with engineering. any objections to timeline: draft template by tomorrow, eng review by Friday?

sam_k: sounds good. i'll start the bench harness changes and add the quant-tolerant tag to model metadata.

product-ops: will draft the ops playbook for pin escape hatch and capacity tagging, cc @maya when ready.

maya: thanks all — keeping this short. will post PR to the onboarding playbook and link to this thread. :rocket:
